The test image shows a close-up of a soybean leaf with:
- Pale/light green irregular patches against the darker green background
- Small dark specks scattered on the surface
- The pale areas appear somewhat angular, following leaf vein patterns

This pattern of pale patches on a leaf surface narrows candidates to: Downy mildew, Powdery mildew, or possibly Bacterial blight. Let me check a Downy mildew reference.

The Downy mildew reference shows small discrete yellow-green spots scattered across leaves. The test image is different — it shows large, diffuse pale/whitish irregular patches covering much of the leaf, with small dark specks. This pattern of whitish powdery-looking patches with dark specks is more consistent with **Powdery Mildew**, which begins as small white patches that coalesce, with the dark specks potentially being cleistothecia (fungal reproductive structures).
